name: City Council Meeting
minutes_text:
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  May 19, 2014

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Kelley at 5:02 p.m., on May 19, 2014, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on May 14, 2014, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the
Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Reardon
  Council Member Schlicht
  Council Member Ury (arrived at 8:16 p.m.)
  Mayor Pro Tem Leckness
  Mayor Kelley

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Public Employee Performance Evaluation of the Incumbent for the Position of City
  Manager Pursuant to Government Code Sections 54957 and 54957.6

CS2. Conference with City Attorney Concerning One matter of Existing Litigation
  Pursuant to Government Code Section 54956.9. The Litigation is state City of
  Mission Viejo; Successor Agency to the Community Development Agency of the City
  of Mission Viejo v. the State of California; California Director of Finance; California
  State Controller; Orange County Auditor-Controller. Case No. 34-2014-80001829.

City Council Minutes  1  May 19, 2014
 RECESS

At the hour of 5:02 p.m., Mayor Kelley recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City
Council reconvened at 6:06 p.m. with four City Council Members present (Council Member Ury
was absent.)

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Pro Tem Leckness

INVOCATION: Council Member Schlicht

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Recognizing May 26 through September 1, 2014 as "Drowning Prevention and
  Awareness"

  Mayor Kelley presented the proclamation to OCFA Battalion Chief Terry Scortt.

P2.  Featured Business of the Month - High Park Tap House

  Mayor Kelley presented the proclamation to John and Valorie Green, owners of the High
  Park Tap House.

P3.  School Spotlight - Montevideo Elementary

  The City Council received the presentation from Montevideo Principal Mona
  Montgomery.

P4.  School Spotlight - Bathgate Elementary

  The City Council received the presentation from Bathgate Principal Shelly Kurtz.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

David Cummings, M.V.: asked the City Council to look into the idea of building a city
gymnasium, not just for basketball but for other sports and to generate rental income.

Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: expressed concern with the City's liability exposure if the Orange
County Fire Authority were to go bankrupt.

Andy Li, M.V.: announced that he is the owner and general manager of Grand Garden China
Bistro in Foothill Marketplace and he is excited to join the community. He noted that the City’s
building and planning staff helped him a lot and it felt like a city he wanted to do business in.
City Council Minutes  2  May 19, 2014
 Joe Tully, M.V.: stated that in 2006, it was determined that there are a lack of public restrooms in
city parks. He noted that the Community Services Commission and the City Council
unanimously approved a restroom master and while one park was improved, there is a lot more
to be done. Mr. Tully expressed concern about priorities and asked the Council to get the stalled
program back in process.

Margot Ferron, M.V.: representing the American Cancer Society and Relay for Life, she invited
residents to a Roaring 20s Survivors’ Dinner Dance on May 21 from 6:00 to 9:00 p.m. at the
community center. She also presented Mayor Kelley with an American Cancer Society award
for Mission Viejo’s Relay for Life efforts in 2013 and she invited residents to this year’s Relay,
June 7-8, 2014.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 13, 15, 17 and 18 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion.

Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Leckness, seconded by Council Member Reardon, to approve
the Consent Calendar as described below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Schlicht
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  Ury

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles
  which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and
  further reading waived.

2.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of May 5, 2014, as presented.

3.  Check Register dated May 2, 2014 in the amount of $886,619.94

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  Quarterly Check Registers and Quarterly Cash Receipts Report - Third Quarter of
  FY 2013-14

  Received and filed.

City Council Minutes  3  May 19, 2014
 5.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for March 2014

  Received and filed.

6.  Mission Viejo Community Development Financing Authority (MVCDFA) Treasurer’s
  Monthly Report for March 2014

  Received and filed.

  Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer’s Monthly Report for March
7.  2014

  Received and filed.

8.  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly
  Report for March 2014

  Received and filed.

9.  Marguerite Parkway Civic Core Median Island Landscape Improvements from
  Estanciero to Via Florecer (CIP 799) - Notice of Completion

  (1) Authorized the City Clerk to record Notice of Completion with the County of Orange
  and to release the faithful performance and payment bond one year and 35 days
  respectively after the date of recordation of the Notice of Completion contingent upon no
  claims or liens being filed with or by the City and (2) authorized the payment of the final
  retention of $17,397.21 35 days after the date of recordation of the Notice of Completion.

10. 2014 Fourth of July Community Street Faire

  Approved the Special Events Permit submitted by the Mission Viejo Activities Committee
  authorizing the annual Mission Viejo Fourth of July Community Street Faire on Friday,
  July 4, 2014.

11. Annual Review of Residential and Commercial Integrated Waste Management Rates

  Adopted Resolution 14-15 Approving the Proposed Trash Rate Adjustment for Residential
  (1.11% Increase From $12.65 to $12.79 per Month), Commercial (1.10% Increase), and
  Roll-Off (1.09% Increase) Services Effective July 1, 2014.

12. La Paz Road Median Island Runoff Prevention Project (CIP 216)-Notice of
  Completion

  (1) Certified the completion of and accepted the improvements for the subject project; (2)
  authorized the City Manager to sign the Notice of Completion; (3) authorized the City
  Clerk to record the Notice of Completion with the County of Orange and to release the
  faithful performance and payment bonds one year and 35 days, respectively, after the date
City Council Minutes  4  May 19, 2014
   of recordation of the Notice of Completion contingent upon no claims or liens being filed
  with the City; and (4) authorized payment of the final retention 35 days after the date of
  recordation of the Notice of Completion.

14. Oso Parkway Widening, I-5 Freeway to Country Club Drive (CIP 791)

  Awarded the contract in the amount of $3,481,376.71 to C.S. Legacy Construction, Inc., for
  construction of the subject project.

16. 2014 Residential Resurfacing-CDBG Asphalt Repairs and Asphalt Overlays (CIP 838)

  Approved the bid specifications, subject to minor revisions required by the City Engineer,
  and authorized staff to advertise for construction bids for the subject project.

19. Quarterly Financial Report for the City of Mission Viejo -- Third Quarter of 2013-14

  Received and filed.

20. La Paz Bridge and Road Widening, Muirlands to Chrisanta (CIP 756/761)-Grant
  Funding Extension

  Adopted Resolution 14-17 Authorizing the City Manager to Request an Extension of Time
  from the Orange County Transportation Authority for Funding for the La Paz Bridge and
  Road Widening Project (CIP 756/761).

PUBLIC HEARINGS

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

17. Reissuance of the Variance to Municipal Code 97-169 for Casta del Sol Homeowners
  Association

18. Reissuance of the Variance to Municipal Code 97-169 for Palmia Homeowners
  Association

  Public Services Administrative Manager Paul Catsimanes presented the staff report for
  agenda items 17 and 18.

  The following spoke in support of the use of firearms, under controlled conditions, to
  eradicate rabbits within Casta del Sol: Carol Weidler, M.V.

  The following spoke in opposition to the use of firearms to eradicate rabbits: Delores
  Denton, M.V. and Patricia Dick, M.V.

  Motion made by Council Member Reardon, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Leckness, to
  authorize staff to reissue the variance to the Casta del Sol Homeowners Association and the
  Palmia Homeowners Association for Municipal Code Firearm Ordinance 97-169.
City Council Minutes  5  May 19, 2014
   On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Schlicht
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Ury

OLD BUSINESS

21. Details of the City of Laguna Niguel’s Action to Declare E-Cigarette Stores as
  Specialty Retail

  Director of Community Development Elaine Lister presented the staff report and answered
  the City Council Members questions.

  The City Council received and filed the report.

NEW BUSINESS

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR (Continued)

13. Muirlands Boulevard Street Lights

  Director of Public Works Mark Chagnon presented the staff report.

  Council Member Schlicht stated that we are still not in the best of financial times and she feels
  there are greater needs elsewhere.

  Motion made by Council Member Reardon, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Leckness, to (1)
  adopt Resolution 14-16 Amending the Fiscal Year 2013-2014 Budget to Create Capital
  Improvement Project 222 to Construct the Muirlands Boulevard Street Light Improvements.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, and Reardon
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  Ury

  Council Member Reardon asked staff to notify residents in the area of the street light additions.

15. Sierra Recreation Center Play Area (CIP 323)

  Jerry Hill, Public Services Operations Manager, presented the staff report and answered the
  City Council Members questions. Mr. Hill also shared photographs of the proposed
  playground equipment.

  Council Member Ury arrived at 8:16 p.m.

City Council Minutes  6  May 19, 2014
   Ryan Hammett, M.V.: asked the City Council to table the matter until gym members can be
  polled for their opinions on the proposed play area.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Council Member Reardon, to (1)
  approve the Plans and Specifications and authorize staff to advertise for bids for the Sierra
  Recreation Center Play Area (CIP) 323, and (2) direct staff to conduct an informal survey
  of recreation center members to assess interest in installation of a play area, and report back
  to the City Council the 3rd week in June.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

22. Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: discussed the Workmen’s Comp situation at OCFA. He stated
  that claims are skyrocketing and he has submitted a report to the District Attorney who he
  hopes will follow up on the matter.

  Mayor Kelley presented the report.

23. Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Council Member Reardon presented the report.

24. San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Council Member Reardon presented the report.

25. Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA)

  Council Member Ury presented the report.

26. Orange County Vector Control District

  Council Member Leckness presented the report.

City Council Minutes  7  May 19, 2014
 STAFF REPORTS

City Manager’s Report

City Manager Wilberg provided the Council with an update on the problems with the council
chamber sound system. He noted that audio experts have evaluated the equipment and
determined that there are four bad units. The sound system has been jerry rigged because parts
are no longer available and prices for new equipment were very high. Staff is continuing to seek
quotes and is looking at options for repairing the sound system.

City Attorney’s Report

City Attorney Curley announced that he had nothing to report.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

27. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as presented
  in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public record.

Council Member Reardon

Council Member Reardon announced that she attended a pancake breakfast fundraiser at
Esperanza, a school for special needs children and adults up to 21 years of age. She noted that
the La Paz Jazz Band played at the event and they were unbelievable. She asked Mayor Kelley
to invite the Principal of Esperanza to come to an upcoming Council meeting and provide a
school spotlight. Council Member Reardon reminded residents of the City's Memorial Day
ceremony on May 26 at the Civic Center at 8:30 a.m. She stated that the City always does an
amazing job and she invited residents to come out and see the American Heroes banners which
are currently on display outside of city hall. She noted that her Godson met Megan McClung in
Iraq the day before she died, and Ms. McClung is featured on one of the American Heroes
banners. She also shared the story of a staff member who met Megan McClung's childhood
friend as she viewed the banners with her family recently. Council Member Reardon noted that
Megan's own family comes out for the City's Memorial Day ceremony each year and these are
the stories that provide her a reminder that the banners depict real people with real families with
real stories.

Council Member Schlicht

Council Member Schlicht announced that she has done some preliminary research on the HERO
home energy loan program. Her basic research reveals that the program is not right for Mission
Viejo because it attaches to a resident's property taxes and it becomes detrimental to a senior
loan. If the resident wants to refinance or buy a house in a HERO program community, that loan
could quite possibly cost homeowners more. She noted that equity diminishes and risk
increases. Council Member Schlicht stated that it's a clever program and seems to be beneficial
City Council Minutes  8  May 19, 2014
 to the company managing it, but it would put the entire community at risk of paying higher
mortgage rates because the City would be considered a HERO Program community. Council
Member Schlicht outlined her attendance at recent events including a Robert Ming meet and
greet event, Esperanza School's pancake breakfast fundraiser, and a Saddleback Republican
Assembly meeting where she was the guest speaker. During that presentation, she presented
information on the subject of fire maps and she noted that the City Council rejected, repackaged
and renamed the fire zone maps into a Special Fire Protection Area (SFPA.) She stated that
along with that, came problems with desirability and property values. She also expressed
concern to the SRA members that half the city is within this SFPA and she asked what OCFA
has done to protect residents as far as additional equipment or manpower. Council Member
Schlicht announced that the American Legion Post 862 Memorial Day pancake breakfast will be
held on May 24 at the Norman P. Murray Community Center from 7:00 a.m. to 11:00 a.m. and
she invited residents to the City's Memorial Day observance beginning at 8:30 a.m. at the Civic
Center. Council Member Schlicht concluded with a quote from Galileo: "All truths are easy to
understand once they are discovered; the point is to discover them."

Council Member Ury

Council Member Ury announced that he has a son graduating from high school and another one
from 8th grade and it is going to be a very busy time of year with all of the celebrations. He
wished residents well with their own graduation festivities over the next few weeks.

Mayor Pro Tem Leckness

Mayor Pro Tem Leckness told Council Member Reardon that he is glad she is back from her
medical leave and he welcomed the City's new Director of Recreation and Community Services,
Mark Nix.

Mayor Kelley

28.  20th Annual Relay For Life of Mission Viejo

  Mayor Kelley presented her report.

  Motion made by Mayor Kelley, seconded by Council Member Reardon, to declare June as
  Relay For Life Month and direct staff to light the civic center area in purple and display
  purple flags during the month of June.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

City Council Minutes  9  May 19, 2014
 Mayor Kelley introduced Director of Recreation and Community Services Mark Nix and Mr.
Nix shared a bit of background on himself, noting that he grew up in Mission Viejo, is raising his
own children here and he is very happy to be working for the City now. Mayor Kelley reminded
residents that the KSBR birthday bash will be held on May 25, 2014, and tickets can be
purchased on the KSBR website. She also announced that the City's Memorial Day ceremony
will be held on Monday, May 26, 2014, at 8:30 a.m. in front of City Hall. Colonel Russell, the
commanding officer of Mission Viejo's adopted marine battalion, will be speaking as well as
Tom Spry, a veteran and hero. Mayor Kelley invited residents to come and see the display of 50
American Heroes tribute banners, which honor men and women who lost their lives during
service to our nation. The banners are on display at the Civic Center and she noted that we need
to look at the faces and be reminded that we can never take freedom for granted. She also
announced that the Orange County Triathlon will be held on June 1 at Lake Mission Viejo.
Mayor Kelley shared the news of a new business in town, Rejoice Christian Bookstore on Via
Fabricante and she noted that it will be a really welcome addition to the community. She also
outlined her attendance at recent events including the Elks Lodge scholarship presentation
ceremony and the City's job fair where there were 750 job opportunities available. She discussed
the new Mission Viejo Today program she filmed on drowning prevention and where she
interviewed the family of a 22 month-old child who drowned and was revived. Mayor Kelley
stated that it is a very moving topic and it is so important for residents to watch, especially if they
have children. She also filmed a show on the Mock DUI crash program during which she
interviewed Steve Concialdi, President and founder of Friends Against Drinking and Driving and
organizer of the Mock DUI crashes. The program reenacts a drunk driving accident with high
school student actors and it is a very moving and effective presentation that comes to Mission
Viejo high schools every other year. Mayor Kelley encouraged the community to watch both of
the shows and be warned about personal safety for themselves and for their children.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 9:45 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Kelley adjourned the meeting to Monday, June 2, 2014, at 5:00 p.m.

_________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of June 2, 2014

City Council Minutes  10  May 19, 2014
